one_line: Caches one parsed JWK set with a monotonic timestamp and optional expiry.
covers: Storing, clearing, retrieving and expiring one parsed JWK set.
excludes: JWK JSON parsing, key selection, cryptographic verification and HTTP fetching.

flows.name: Store a parsed set
flows.description: Cache a non-None set with a fresh timestamp wrapper.

steps.what_happens: put receives the set and constructs PyJWTSetWithTimestamp.
The wrapper stores the set and captures time.monotonic().

flows.name: Read cached state
flows.description: Reject empty or expired state and otherwise return the stored set.

steps.what_happens: get returns None for an empty cache or when is_expired is true.
get_jwk_set returns the cached set for the unexpired branch.

touchpoints.role: Owns stored cache state and expiration decisions.
Stores the parsed set and its monotonic insertion timestamp.

invariants.rule: The cache constructor starts with no stored timestamp wrapper.
The constructor retains the supplied lifespan without validating its sign.
put(None) clears the stored timestamp wrapper.
invariants.why: The else branch assigns None to jwk_set_with_timestamp.

invariants.rule: put() with a non-None set creates a new PyJWTSetWithTimestamp wrapper.
invariants.why: The non-None branch constructs the wrapper for that set.

invariants.rule: The timestamp wrapper retains the supplied JWK set object.
invariants.why: Its constructor assigns the argument to self.jwk_set.

invariants.rule: The timestamp wrapper records time.monotonic() when constructed.
invariants.why: Its timestamp is assigned by calling time.monotonic().
It returns self.timestamp without refreshing it.

invariants.rule: get_jwk_set returns the stored JWK set.
invariants.why: It returns self.jwk_set without creating a copy.

invariants.rule: get() returns None when the cache is empty.
invariants.why: The initial None condition returns before reading the wrapper.

invariants.rule: is_expired() returns False when the cache is empty.
invariants.why: Its first conjunct requires a non-None timestamp wrapper.

invariants.rule: Lifespans less than or equal to -1 disable expiration for stored entries.
Expiration requires the current monotonic time to be strictly greater than timestamp plus lifespan.
An entry is not expired at exact equality with timestamp plus lifespan.
invariants.why: The strict greater-than comparison is False at equality.

invariants.rule: get() returns None for an expired stored entry.
get() returns the stored set for a present unexpired entry.
invariants.why: It calls the stored wrapper get_jwk_set().

invariants.rule: Returning None for expiration does not itself clear the stored wrapper.
invariants.why: get() performs no assignment before the expired return.

pitfalls.risk: A lifespan at or below -1 leaves stored entries without expiration.
pitfalls.consequence: Elapsed monotonic time alone cannot make is_expired return True for those lifespan values.

entry_questions: Should this change affect clearing, the expiry boundary, or retention of the stored set?
